Short title, extent and commencement

ORDINANCE XXXV OF 1997
ORDINANCE XXXV OF 1997
ELECTRONIC MEDIA REGULATORY
AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance to regulate electronic
media in Pakistan
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary,
Part I, 15th February, 1997]
No.F.2(1)97‑Pub., dated 14‑2‑1997.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:‑‑
Whereas it is necessary to provide
for the development of electronic media in order to improve the standards of
information, education and entertainment and to enlarge the choice available to
the people of Pakistan in the media for news, current affairs, religious
knowledge, art, culture, science technology economic development, social sector
concerns, music, sports, drama and other subjects of public and national
interest;
And Whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
PRELIMINARY
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.‑‑(1)
This Ordinance shall be called the Electronic Media Regulatory Authority
Ordinance, 1997.
(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Definitions

ORDINANCE XXXV OF 1997
ORDINANCE XXXV OF 1997

AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1997

Whereas it is necessary to provide
for the development of electronic media in order to improve the standards of

the people of Pakistan in the media for news, current affairs, religious
knowledge, art, culture, science technology economic development, social sector
concerns, music, sports, drama and other subjects of public and national
interest;

render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
PRELIMINARY
2. Definitions.‑‑In this Ordinance,
unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context:‑‑
(1) "advertisement" means
a set of visual audio messages for the projection of a product, service or idea
with the object of propagating sale, purchase or hire of the product, service
or idea for creating other related effects;
(2) "authority" means the
Electronic Media Regulatory Authority established under section 3 of this
Ordinance.
(3) "broadcasting" means
transmission by radio, television fibre optic or laser system, basic or, pay
cable, super, pay‑over‑the air, pay‑preview, subscription or
closed circuit television individual television fixed service, point to point
microwave relay, direct broadcasting, multipoint or multipoint multichannel
distribution, satellite master antenna television system, satellite service,
cyberspace and any other technology and media now existing or hereafter
developed for viewing or listening by electronic means;
(4) "channel" means the
set of frequencies that a broadcast station occupies for broadcasting;
(5) "company" means a
company as defined in the Companies Ordinance, 1984;
(6) "copyright" means
copyright as defined in the Copyright Ordinance, 1962 and the Copyright Rules,
1967;
(7) "director" in relation
to a firm means a partner of the firm.
(8) "frequency" means
frequency of the electromagnetic wave number measured in Hertz per second and used
for transmission;
(9) "Frequency Allocation
Board" means the Board constituted under the Pakistan Telecommunications
(Re‑organization) Act, 1996;
(10) "license" means a
license issued by the Authority for the establishment and operation of a
broadcast station;
(11) "licensee" means a
person who has been issued a broadcast license by the Authority;
(12) "national
broadcaster" means the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation, the Pakistan
Television Corporation and the Shalimar Recording and Broadcasting Company;
(13) "person" includes an
individual, partnership, association, joint stock company trust or corporation;
(14) "programme" means
systematic broadcasting of visual or sound images by a broadcast station but
does not include an advertisement;
(15) "public service
message" means a set of visual or audio messages for the projection of a
product, service or idea with the object of propagating the product, service or
idea in the public interest;
(16) "rules" means rules
made under this Ordinance; and
(17) "subscriber" means a
person who receives broadcasting from a broadcast station.

Establishment of Authority

3. Establishment of Authority.‑‑(1) The Federal
Government shall establish in accordance with the provision of this Ordinance,
the Electronic Media Regulatory Authority.
(2) The Authority shall be a body
corporate with perpetual succession and the power to hold and dispose of
property and may in its name sue and be sued.

Members of Authority

4. Members of Authority.‑‑(1) The Authority
shall consist of a Chairman and six members appointed by the President of
Pakistan.
(2) The Chairman of the Authority
shall be a retired Judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan.
(3) The six members shall include
the Secretary, Ministry of Information and Media Development and the Secretary,
Ministry of Communications and four Members from the general public including
one with an acknowledged record of work in radio, one with an acknowledged
record of work in television, one with an acknowledge record of public service
and one with an acknowledged record of work in the print media.

Tenure of members

following Ordinance:‑‑

5. Tenure of members.‑‑(1) The Chairman and
Members shall be appointed for a term of four years and shall not be removed
before the expiry of their tenure except for misconduct or prolonged ill
health.
Explanation: "Misconduct"
shall mean conviction of an offence involving moral turpitude, and shall
include conduct prejudicial to good order or unbecoming of a member and a
gentleman.
(2) The Chairman and non‑official
members shall not be eligible for reappointment.

responsible for regulating the establishment and operation of all privately
owned broadcast stations and the development of electronic media in Pakistan.

(2) The Authority may, with the
previous approval of the Federal Government, raise additional funds from
sources other than the Federal Government.

8. License to Broadcast.‑‑(1) The Authority
shall have the exclusive right to issue licenses for the establishment and
operation of all privately owned broadcast stations.
(2) No person shall broadcast except
in accordance with a license issued under this Ordinance.
(3) Every such license shall be
subject to the terms and conditions prescribed by this Ordinance and the rules.
(4) The Authority shall have the
power to charge fee at such rates as the Authority may fix from time to time
for the grant of a license and for its annual renewal.

Terms and conditions of license

Now, therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
PRELIMINARY
9. Terms and conditions of license.‑‑A Broadcaster who is
issued a license under this Ordinance shall;
(1) promote respect for the sovereignty,
security and integrity of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan;
(2) promote respect for the national
cultural and religious values as enshrined in the Objective Resolution;
(3) promote respect for the
principles of public policy as enshrined in the Constitution;
(4) ensure that his programmes and
advertisements do not encourage violence, terrorism, racial discrimination,
religious sectarianism or hatred;
(5) promote respect for law, order
and justice;
(6) allow rejoinder by person
aggrieved by broadcasting which has referred to them by name;
(7) comply with Rules made under
this Ordinance;
(8) broadcast programmes specified
by the Federal Government or the Authority in the manner indicated by
Government or, as the case may be, the Authority;
(9) comply with the code of
Programme Conduct approved by the Authority;
(10) comply with the Code of
Advertisement Conduct approved by the Federal Government;
(11) not broadcast any programme or
advertisement in violation of any copy right or other property right;
(12) obtain license from the
Frequency Allocation Board before import of any transmitting apparatus for
broadcasting; and
(13) not sell, transfer or assign
any of the rights conferred by the license without prior written permission of
the Authority.

Exclusion of Private Monopolies

10. Exclusion of Private Monopolies.‑‑(1) No person other
than a national broadcaster shall be entitled to the benefit of any monopoly or
exclusivity in the matter of broadcasting or the establishment and operation of
broadcast stations or in the supply to, or purchase from a national broadcaster
of air time, programmes or advertising material.
(2) All existing agreements and
contracts conferring a monopoly or containing an exclusivity clause shall be
null and void to the extent of the repugnancy with subsection(1).
(3) In granting a license, the
Authority shall ensure that undue concentration of media ownership is not
created in any city, town or area and the country as a whole by virtue of the
applicant for a broadcast license already owning or operating as sole or joint
shareholder, any other radio station, TV station, printed newspaper or
magazine.

11. License, Application, Issuance,
Refusal, Validity.‑‑(1)
Any person desirous of obtaining a license for broadcasting and for establishment
and operation of a broadcast station shall apply to the Authority in such
manner and form as may be prescribed by rules.
(2) The Authority shall process each
application in accordance with criteria prescribed by rules and shall hold
public hearing before granting or refusing the license.
(3) Each application shall be
accompanied by such fee as may be prescribed by the Authority.
(4) A broadcasting license shall be
valid for a period of five years subject to payment of the annual fee
prescribed by the Authority.
(5) The Authority shall have power
to renew a license on terms and conditions prescribed for renewal or to refuse
renewal for stated reasons.

12. Restrictions of license
ownership.‑‑A
license shall not be granted to:‑‑
(a) a person who is not a national
of Pakistan or resident in Pakistan;
(b) a company organized under the
laws of any foreign Government;
(c) a company the majority of whose
shares are owned or controlled by foreign national or companies.

13. Suspension of broadcasting
operation.‑‑(1)
A broadcaster or operator shall not cease or suspend broadcasting except on
account of force majeure or with the prior approval of the Authority.

Power to authorize inspection

14. Power to authorize inspection.‑‑(1) The Authority may
authorize any officer of the Federal Government or the Authority to enter the
premises of broadcaster for inspection and search.
(2) A broadcast station shall, at
all reasonable times, be open to inspection and search by an authorized officer
under subsection (1) and the licensee shall provide such officer with every
assistance and facility in performing his duties.
(3) The authorized officer shall
within 7 days of the inspections, submit his inspection report to the
Authority.

15. Prohibition of Broadcasts.‑‑The Authority shall by
order prohibit any broadcaster from broadcasting or re‑broadcasting any
programme if it feels that such particular programme is likely to create hatred
among the people or is prejudicial to the maintenance of law and order or
likely to disturb public peace and tranquillity, or endangers national
security.

Power to vary conditions, suspend or revoke the licence

16. Power to vary conditions,
suspend or revoke the licence.‑‑(1) The Authority may, during the currency of a license,
by notice in writing vary or revoke or add to any of the conditions upon which
the license has been granted.
(2) The Authority may revoke or
suspend the license of a broadcaster on one or more of the following grounds,
namely;
(a) the licensee has failed to pay
the license fee and related charges;
(b) the licensee has contravened any
provision of this Ordinance;
(c) the licensee has failed to
comply with any condition of the license or any direction given by the
Authority;
(d) reasons of necessity in the
public interest; and
(e) if the share‑holders or
directors of the licensee, being a company, have transferred the majority of
their shares.
(3) Except for reason of necessity
in the public interest a license shall not be suspended or cancelled unless the
licensee has been given reasonable notice to show cause.

PRELIMINARY
17. Offences and penalties.‑‑(1) Any broadcaster or
person who violates or abets the violation of any of the provisions of this
Ordinance shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to
five years and with fine not exceeding one million rupees.
(2) Enhanced fine and imprisonment
in case or subsequent offences.
Where any broadcastor or person
convicted for an offence is again convicted for the same offence, the penalties
and imprisonment imposed may be 'double to those awarded in the original
instance.

following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:‑‑
Whereas it is necessary to provide
for the development of electronic media in order to improve the standards of
information, education and entertainment and to enlarge the choice available to
the people of Pakistan in the media for news, current affairs, religious
knowledge, art, culture, science technology economic development, social sector
concerns, music, sports, drama and other subjects of public and national
interest;
And Whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;

Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑

19. Offences by companies.‑‑Where any offence,
under this Ordinance has been committed by a company, every person who at the
time, the offence was committed, was incharge of and was responsible to the
company for, the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company
shall be deemed to be guilty of such offence and shall be liable to be
proceeded against and punished accordingly.

No.F.2(1)97‑Pub., dated 14‑2‑1997.‑‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:‑‑
Whereas it is necessary to provide
for the development of electronic media in order to improve the standards of
information, education and entertainment and to enlarge the choice available to
the people of Pakistan in the media for news, current affairs, religious
knowledge, art, culture, science technology economic development, social sector
concerns, music, sports, drama and other subjects of public and national
interest;
And Whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
PRELIMINARY
20. Power to make rules.‑‑The Authority may,
with the approval of Government, by notification in the official Gazette, make
rules and to carry out the purposes of this Ordinance, including:‑‑
(a) to prescribe the forms for
licenses for working, installing or dealing in transmission broadcast apparatus
and the manner in which application for the licenses shall be granted;
(b) to prescribe the terms and
conditions of the license; and
(c) to prescribe standards and
measures for the establishment of broadcasting station, installation of
broadcast equipment, transmitter, receivers, boosters, converters and common
antennae.
